div.head: VIIa Atr Inscr.
div.ab: Ðis man gerædde, ða se micele here com to lande.
Ðis man gerædde ða se micele here com to lande.
This edict was drawn up when the great army came to the country.
This was decreed when the great army came to the country.
Dies wurde beschlossen, als das grosse [Nordische] Heer ins Land kam.
This was decided when the great [Norse] army came to the land.
div.note: Only MS: D (CCCC 201 p. 30, after homilies, the last being the so-called Wulfstan ed. Napier no. 38, in the same hand, c. 1075). K now gives Liebermann's text from D. The heading is in red and not part of the law. Napier corrects ‘micele’ to ‘micela’. Dated 992–1011 (Bath penitential edict).
This rubric is only in the Old English version; the Latin says instead that this was decreed by King Ethelred and his councillors at Bath.
